skillSummaries.frontend: I build React, Next.js, and TypeScript interfaces meant to last: reusable component boundaries, deliberate state management — Redux Toolkit when the data calls for it — complex forms, responsive layouts, and rendering kept under control performance-wise. I cover them with unit tests using Jest, Vitest, and React Testing Library, testing behaviour rather than implementation: on a high-volume sales tracking application, more than 80% coverage sustained over two years. I have also shipped Angular applications to production, and I do the Figma mockups myself when a project has no designer.
skillSummaries.backend: I design and expose REST APIs with Node.js and Next.js, over a PostgreSQL or Supabase data model thought through up front rather than inherited by accident: schema, constraints, multi-tenant isolation through RLS. Around it come authentication and roles — OAuth 2.0, SSO, token lifecycle — payments, asynchronous background processing, event-driven microservice architectures when the load calls for them, and third-party integrations, SharePoint and Yousign included. I can also pick up an existing back-end, Java EE included, and move it forward without destabilising what already runs.
skillSummaries.cloud_devops: I deploy and operate what I build: Vercel, Firebase, and Google Cloud, with CI/CD pipelines that replay the test suite before every release. I favour small, frequent releases that are easy to verify and to roll back over large, ceremonial deployments — and I watch the KPIs afterwards, because a shipped feature is not yet a feature that serves anyone.
skillSummaries.data_ml: I integrate language models where they hold up their end of the bargain: assistants and search over business data, content generation constrained by a strict schema and therefore verifiable, agents that call real tools through the MCP protocol. The technical problem is always the same — framing a non-deterministic output so it becomes usable data, with a human review wherever a mistake is expensive. Coming from research at the Grenoble Computer Science Laboratory, where I trained convolutional neural networks with PyTorch and integrated the resulting model into a Pepper robot, I kept the ability to read a paper, understand a model, and honestly assess what an AI component does — or does not — bring to a product.
skillSummaries.tools_methods: Code gets written in TDD: the test first, the implementation after, and a suite that runs in continuous integration before every release — unit tests with Jest and Vitest, end-to-end with Playwright. Git every day, demanding and well-argued code reviews, documentation written for whoever picks the project up after me. On an Agile team — Scrum, SAFe, PI Plannings — I estimate, split work into shippable increments, demo every week, and raise blockers early rather than on demo day. Coding assistants are part of the toolkit, provided what they produce gets read line by line.
skillSummaries.soft_skills: Autonomous on unfamiliar ground: I frame the need, ask the right people the right questions, and move forward without needing to be chased. On several engagements I was the only technical contact, from the first scoping session to the go-live — which means estimating honestly, holding the date I announced, and talking about the product with people who do not write code. Curious and rigorous, I keep up with the ecosystem, gladly pass on what I learn, and work naturally with product, design, and the teams already in place.

about.name: Léo Bello
about.title: Full-Stack Developer — React, Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL
about.bio:
Full-stack developer, seven years spent on applications that are not allowed to break: sales performance tracking across 29,000 points of sale for La Française des Jeux, an invoicing SaaS used in more than fifty countries, a rental management application written from scratch in TDD. I take a product from the interface down to the database, or I pick up an existing one — its debt, its overdue upgrades, its slowness — and ship it tested, documented, and ready for the next developer to take over.

What I build: dashboards, back-offices, customer portals, MVPs. On the interface side, React, Next.js, and TypeScript — component architecture, state management, complex forms, rendering kept under control performance-wise. On the server side, REST APIs in Node.js and Next.js over a PostgreSQL or Supabase data model thought through before it is written, and everything around it: authentication and roles, OAuth 2.0 and SSO, payments, third-party integrations, event-driven architectures when the load calls for them, continuous deployment. And AI when it serves the product rather than the pitch: LLM API integration under a strict schema, assistants over business data, tool-calling agents.

What holds it all together comes down to a few things: tests written before the code and more than 80% coverage sustained over time, well-argued code reviews, CI/CD pipelines that replay the suite before every release, a demo every week rather than a grand reveal at the end. Prospeo and SignFlow — two products scoped, built, secured, and shipped single-handedly — are the fullest expression of that.

projects.name: Prospeo

screenshots.caption: Prospect record — SIRET matched against the SIRENE registry, contact details, web presence, and the score broken down line by line.
The same screen in dark theme: the product follows the system theme.

projects.summary: Thousands of tradespeople and small businesses have no website at all, and approaching them one by one costs more than it brings in. Prospeo automates the whole chain: it finds those businesses, builds them a site, puts it online, then sends them a proposal pointing at their own site — already live.
projects.approach: Detection through Google Maps, matching against the SIRENE company registry, and scoring that can be replayed on data already collected — criteria can be refined without crawling again. Copy written by an LLM under a strict schema, automatic Git commit and deployment, every step traced and timestamped. Human review before sending, email and SMS, with a database guarantee that a prospect can never be contacted twice.
projects.outcome: A long, asynchronous, failure-prone business chain held together end to end: background job orchestration, three third-party APIs, AI-generated content constrained by a schema and therefore verifiable, multi-tenant isolation through RLS and encrypted secrets. 52,000 lines, 115 test files.

projects.name: SignFlow

screenshots.caption: The morning brief: today's listings above the threshold, then the whole watch list with its filters.
One listing in detail — its rank, the criteria that produced it, and where the application stands.

projects.summary: Looking for a role means re-reading the same listings across four sites that don't talk to each other, to keep three of them. SignFlow does that re-reading at night: four sources merged, republications of the same offer collapsed into a single entry, and one brief waiting in the morning.
projects.approach: Every offer is read by AI and checked against real criteria — remote work, pay, engagement length, technologies you no longer want to touch. Each ranking comes with its reason, and changing a criterion re-ranks the whole history instantly: the judgement is recomputed, not frozen at collection time.
projects.outcome: Turning a raw feed into a decision: normalising heterogeneous sources, reliable deduplication, AI judgement that is reproducible and auditable, and a data model that accepts rule changes after the fact. Nothing is sent without approval — the product prepares the decision, it does not take it.

experience.role: Full-Stack Developer React / Next.js — built from scratch, freelance
experience.description:
A seasonal rental management application built from scratch, from requirements gathering to production: technical architecture and data model defined from zero, with no existing codebase to inherit.

Fully developed with TDD — React / TypeScript front-end, Next.js back-end on Supabase and PostgreSQL — on a microservices, event-driven architecture designed to scale. Third-party integrations with SharePoint and Yousign, OAuth 2.0 / SSO authentication with full token lifecycle management.

A scope owned end to end rather than a single brick handed over: UX/UI mockups, tests written before the code, technical documentation, and deployment through CI/CD pipelines.

experience.role: Research Intern in Computer Science — computer vision and robotics
